summary: 1. ** - July 9 total production 23,467 BCM against a 23,469.2 BCM target — essentially on plan (−2.2 BCM). 2. Ore ran 77% over target for a second straight day, and **MTD ore turned positive for the first time this month: +997.1 BCM (+3.9%)**, after running behind plan every prior day of July. - Crusher fed 3,592 BCM — a new best single-day feed for the July run, beating July 8's 3,416 BCM. - **DR-139 partially recovered**, from a full 24-hour, both-shift breakdown on July 8 to a day-shift-only breakdown on July 9 — night shift logged standby instead of continued breakdown. 3. The fault ("Hard breaking troubleshooting in progress") remains open with no Date Out, now day 3. - EX-123 stayed down a fourth straight day ("L.H Track Off"); DT-282 stayed down a third straight day ("Coolant Inlet Pressure Sensor Problem"); DZ-249 stayed down a second day ("Track Spotter Broken"). 4. Two new tyre-fault breakdowns hit the dump truck fleet (DT-128, 22.5 hrs; DT-244, 14.75 hrs), pulling daily dump truck availability down to 89.67% even as the overall fleet daily average (94.45%) and MTD average (91.73%) both hit new highs for the July run. - Blast No. 11 confirmed (890-643 Trim + 639 Remnant, 37,037 BCM, 21,064 kg explosive) — logged as "yesterday's blast" against the July 9 tab, meaning the blast happened July 8. - Day 15 survey reconciliation (260710-INX-SUM, reconciling July 9 production) read −12.4% against the truck tally — a second straight negative day, three excavators on the heap again. 5. MTD survey surplus narrowed to +3.03%, the third straight pass of narrowing (Day 13 +6.0% → Day 14 +4.1% → Day 15 +3.03%).
